prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous ground plane of the outdoor baseball field receding from the camera wearer's feet (~1–1.5 m at the bottom) toward the distant chain-link fence and posts (>8 m in the dark background on the right), though the overall brightness scale shifts unevenly when the camera pitches straight down at the dirt in frames 2–3. It clearly separates the foreground objects within arm's reach (0.3–0.8 m)—specifically the camera wearer's right hand and held baseball bat entering from the bottom-right in frames 2, 3, and 5, plus their left shoe at the bottom of frame 2—from the ground-level baseball glove (~1.5–2 m ahead on the right) and the other person standing ~5–6 m ahead (~3 m beyond home plate). Across the 5 frames, the gradient changes from a receding horizon view (frame 1) to a nearly uniform dark-grey overhead plane as the camera wearer bends and looks down toward the glove and home plate (frames 2–3), then returns to a deep ground gradient in frames 4–5 as the camera tilts up and the bat rises into the bright near-field on the right. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the 3D elevation of the raised bat above the dirt in frame 2 and the vertical silhouette of the distant person and fence posts in frames 4–5 immediately distinct from flat ground markings and shadows. However, it is unreliable for small or low-profile objects: the flat home plate (~2 m ahead) is completely invisible, the baseball glove (~1.5–2 m) and scattered baseballs (~3.5–4.5 m ahead, ~1–1.5 m in front of the other person) barely register as faint bumps, and the other person's upper body is cropped at the top of frame 1 and entirely out of view in frames 2–3.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against the unlabelled dirt field, detecting the distant person (~5–6 m ahead in the upper-centre of frames 1, 4, and 5), the baseball glove on the ground to the front-right (~1.5 m away in frame 1), and the handheld baseball bat within arm's reach (~0.3–0.8 m) in frames 2, 3, and 5. In frame 1, the distant person's lower body is segmented at the top edge (with their torso cropped out of frame) ~4 m behind the segmented glove on the right; in frames 2–3, the camera wearer looks down so the distant person leaves the view while the bat, right hand, and left shoe at the bottom edge are segmented; and in frames 4–5, the camera tilts back up to show the full silhouette of the person ~5–6 m ahead bending forward at the waist toward the camera wearer while the bat re-enters on the bottom-right. This map makes it easy to track the exact pixel boundaries of the bat+hand/shoe unit in frame 2 and the distant person's compact bent-over silhouette in frames 4–5 without being distracted by the strong dark ground shadows in the RGB image. However, the map is highly unreliable in both recall and classification: it misses the baseball glove entirely in frames 2 and 3 despite it remaining ~1.5–2 m ahead on the right, and it fails to detect home plate (~2 m ahead) or any of the ~8–9 baseballs scattered on the dirt ~3.5–4.5 m away (~1–1.5 m in front of the other person). Furthermore, it mislabels the camera wearer's own shoe at the bottom of frame 2 as part of the 'baseball bat', misclassifies the bat handle and hand at the bottom-left of frame 3 as a 'person', and mislabels the raised bat barrel on the right of frame 5 as 'skis'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders a 2D yellow body skeleton only in frames 4 and 5 for the person standing ~5–6 m in front of the camera wearer, while leaving frames 1–3 completely blank. In frames 4 and 5, the compact cluster of head, shoulder, hip, knee, and ankle keypoints shows that this person is stationary, facing toward the camera wearer, and bent sharply forward at the waist with their head lowered below shoulder level, looking down at the cluster of baseballs ~1–1.5 m in front of their feet rather than up at the camera wearer. From frame 4 to frame 5, the skeleton shifts slightly upward and rightward in image coordinates as the camera wearer tilts their head up and slightly left, while the person's arms hang downward near their knees just above reach of the balls on the dirt. Compared to the RGB strip—where dark clothing, a cap shadow, and foreshortening make the bent torso blend into the legs—the skeleton explicitly disambiguates the relative vertical alignment of the lowered head, shoulders, hips, and legs. However, the pose map is unreliable whenever bodies are partly occluded or cropped: it fails to detect the distant person's visible legs at the top of frame 1, misses the camera wearer's own right hand gripping the bat within arm's reach (0.3–0.5 m) in frames 2, 3, and 5 as well as their left foot in frame 2, and renders no magenta hand keypoints anywhere while collapsing the distant person's left and right limb keypoints nearly on top of each other.
